title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Throughout the notes G is a stable 'type' graph: the dual graph of a stable marked curve, with vertices of given genus and valence ('ordre'), edges, and half-edges. Write $\hat A_s$ for the half-edges at a vertex s. $M_G$ is the corresponding stratum of $\overline{M}_{g,\nu}$. $S_0\mathcal T_G$ and $\mathcal T_G$ are the Teichmüller-type groupoids attached to G, built on the previous page from sets $\mathcal E_a$ and products $P_G=\prod T_a$ of circle-torsors ('fibres unitaires').

This page starts the case of modular dimension 1, i.e. $\dim M_G = 3g-3+n-\#\text{edges} = 1$. Then every vertex except one, $s_0$, is of type (0,3). The exceptional vertex $s_0$ is either of type (0,4) or of type (1,1). These are the two pictures drawn on the page.

The case where $s_0$ has type (0,4):
- Put $I=\hat A_{s_0}$, a set with 4 elements.
- The other components are rigid 3-pointed lines, so $M_G\cong M_{0,I}$. This is $\cong \mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}=U_{0,3}$, but only after choosing a numbering of I.
- A curve X of type G is the same as a projective line Y with points marked by I; the rest of X is canonically determined.
- Canonically, $M_{0,I}=\mathrm{Rep}(I)\wedge^{\mathfrak S_4} M_{0,4}$, a contracted product with the $\mathfrak S_4$-torsor of frames $\mathrm{Rep}(I)=\mathrm{Bij}(I_4,I)$, where $I_4=\{1,2,3,4\}$.
- This equals $\mathrm{Rep}(I)\wedge^{\mathfrak S_4} U_{0,3}$. Here $\mathfrak S_4$ acts on $U_{0,3}$ through $\mathfrak S_4\to\mathfrak S_3$, whose kernel is the Klein group $V_4$.
- $\mathfrak S_3$ is identified with the permutations of the three (2,2)-partitions $P_i=\{\{i,4\},I_3\setminus\{i\}\}$ of $I_4$. These partitions correspond to the three boundary points (cusps) of $\overline M_{0,4}$, i.e. to $0,1,\infty$.

The page then introduces $T_i$ ($i\in I$): the unit tangent circles of Y at the marked points. The aim is to express each $T_a$, and hence the torsor $SP_X=\prod_a T_a$ of the next page, in terms of the $T_i$. The point is to describe $S_0\mathcal T_G$ and $\mathcal T_G$ explicitly for the one-dimensional strata.

Purpose. These are the 'building blocks' $M_{0,4}$ and $M_{1,1}$ of the Teichmüller tower, which the Esquisse says is generated in modular dimension ≤2. The page sets up the dimension-1 pieces of the construction with tangential/circle data at the boundary.
errors: No mathematical errors. The claim that the $\mathfrak S_4$-action on $M_{0,4}$ factors through $\mathfrak S_3$ (the Klein group fixes the cross-ratio) is correct. So is the bijection between the three (2,2)-partitions and the three cusps.

Minor implicit point: $M_G\cong M_{0,I}$ holds at the level of the rigidified (marked-graph) stratum. If G has automorphisms, the actual stratum of $\overline M$ is a quotient. Grothendieck works with the rigidified version throughout, so this is not an error.

ideas.what: Classification of stable graphs of modular dimension 1: all vertices trivalent genus 0 except one of type (0,4) or (1,1)
ideas.modern_name: one-dimensional boundary strata of $\overline M_{g,n}$ (F-curves / 'Lego' level 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore. Used in Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Bakalov–Kirillov (Lego–Teichmüller game), Keel–McKernan (F-curves)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (modular dimension 1 and 2 building blocks)

ideas.what: Canonical description $M_{0,I}=\mathrm{Rep}(I)\wedge^{\mathfrak S_4} U_{0,3}$ with $\mathfrak S_4$ acting through $\mathfrak S_3$ = permutations of the (2,2)-partitions
ideas.modern_name: cross-ratio; $\mathfrak S_4\to\mathfrak S_3$ with Klein kernel acting trivially on $M_{0,4}$

ideas.what: Using unit tangent circles $T_i$ at marked points to build the torsors $T_a$ and the circle-bundle object $SP_X$
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points / real oriented blow-up of the boundary (Kimura–Zagier-type 'frames'), base points at infinity of the Teichmüller groupoid

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine case analysis setting up the dimension-1 strata within Grothendieck's tangential-base-point construction of the Teichmüller groupoid. The broader programme belongs to the known Esquisse circle of ideas, and its tangential-base-point aspects were later developed by others. Nothing on this page itself goes beyond the classical $M_{0,4}$ / cross-ratio description.
transcription_corrections: 'U_{0,3}' is an interlinear insertion above 'iso canonique', and its placement relative to the parenthetical '(≃ P^1_C \ {0,1,∞}' is unclear in the image. Either way, it records that $M_{0,I}\simeq U_{0,3}$ after numbering.
The crossed-out line after $M_G\simeq M_{0,I}$ looks like '$SP_G\simeq$' rather than '$P_G\simeq$'.
The margin note reads 'NB $\mathrm{Rep}(I)=\mathrm{Bij}(I_4,I)$ avec $I_4=\mathbb N\cap[1,4]$'.
The final line 'pour Φ ∈ A' is probably 'pour a ∈ A', with an overwritten symbol. This fits the next page, which treats each edge a.
The target of $\mathfrak S_4\to$ is written like '$\mathfrak S_B$' in the image, but it is meant as $\mathfrak S_3$.
